newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court extends external rule at oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Russian court extends external rule at oil firm.

text.p: A court in Rostov-on-Don in southern Russia extended an order protecting oil marketing company AO Rostovnefteprodukt from creditors until March 1, 1997, a Sidanko spokesman said on Monday.
Rostovnefteprodukt is a sales branch of Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sidanko), one of Russia's dozen vertically integrated oil groups.
Sidanko owns 51 percent of Rostovnefteprodukt voting shares. Its main production units are Chernogorneft, Varyoganneftegaz and Kondpetroleum.

The court decided to prolong the protection from creditors regime, similar to Chapter 11 under U.S. re-organisation rules, after Dmitry Shchukin, the external manager appointed by the court, had asked for it, saying the company needed to pay off all its debts.

He said Rostovnefteprodukt had paid off 31 billion roubles out of 51 billion roubles in debt during 12 months of protection. AO Norsi, a subsidiary of Norsi-Oil from Nizhny Novgorod, is the company's major creditor.
A Rostov regional court declared Rostovnefteprodukt insolvent last year with total debt amounting to over 100 billion roubles and introduced protection from creditors.
A shareholders' meeting last June transferred more than 30 petrol stations out of 40 owned by Rostovnefteprodukt to NIKA, a bank in Rostov-on-Don, which at that time was its main creditor.
Tatyana Gramotenko, head of the local agency for bankruptcy issues, said Rostovnefteprodukt had paid all its debts to the government.
